section.heading: Determination that exceptional circumstances apply in relation to a person

content.p: If:
(a) a person (the affected person) is or was a bonded participant; or
a person is a legal personal representative of an affected person who:
is deceased; or
lacks capacity to make an application under this section;
the affected person, or the legal personal representative, may apply to the Secretary for a determination that exceptional circumstances apply in relation to the affected person.
The application must:
be made in writing; and
set out the exceptional circumstances that apply in relation to the affected person; and
set out any other information specified in the Bonded Medical Program rules; and
be accompanied by any documents specified in the Bonded Medical Program rules.
If an applicant makes an application under subsection (1), the Secretary may determine that exceptional circumstances apply in relation to the affected person.
In determining whether exceptional circumstances apply in relation to the affected person, the Secretary must have regard to any matter specified in the Bonded Medical Program rules.
If the Secretary makes the determination under subsection (3) that exceptional circumstances apply in relation to the affected person, the Secretary must:
give the applicant written notice of the determination; and
state in the notice that the Secretary is satisfied that:
the exceptional circumstances will prevent the affected person from complying with the condition mentioned in paragraph 124ZG(1)(a) or (c); or
the affected person breached a condition mentioned in paragraph 124ZG(1)(a) or (c) as a result of the exceptional circumstances; or
the affected person withdrew from the Bonded Medical Program under section 124ZP as a result of the exceptional circumstances; and
set out, in the notice, the effect of subparagraph 124ZE(4)(b)(vi) and whichever of the following provisions is applicable in relation to the affected person:
subsection 124ZH(4);
subsection 124ZJ(4);
subsection 124ZQ(6).
A statement under subparagraph (5)(b)(ii) or (iii) may relate to a breach of a condition or a withdrawal (as the case may be) that occurs before or after the commencement of this section.
If the Secretary refuses to make the determination under subsection (3) in relation to the affected person, the Secretary must give the applicant written notice of the following:
the decision to refuse to make the determination;
the reasons for the decision;
how the applicant may apply for review of the decision.
If:
a person makes an application under subsection 124ZEA(1); and
the Secretary needs further information to make a decision on the application;
the Secretary may, by written notice, request the person to give further information to the Secretary within a specified period.
The specified period must not be shorter than 28 days after the notice is given.
The Secretary may, at the person’s request, extend the specified period. The request must be made in writing and before that period ends.
If the person does not give the requested further information within:
in a case in which the specified period has been extended under subsection (3)—the period as so extended; or
otherwise—the specified period;
the application is taken to be withdrawn at the end of the period.
A notice given under subsection (1) must set out the effect of subsection (4).

section.heading: Extended compliance determination for certain BMP and MRBS participants

content.p: If:
a person is:
a party to a deed of agreement with the Commonwealth (as represented by the Department) for funding of a place in the Bonded Medical Places Scheme, including a deed of agreement as varied; or
a party to a contract with the Commonwealth (as represented by the Department) for a Medical Rural Bonded Scholarship, including a contract as varied; and
the person meets the requirements specified in the Bonded Medical Program rules;

the person may apply to the Secretary for a determination (the extended compliance determination) that, if the person were to become a bonded participant, the person would be required to complete their return of service obligation within a period that is longer than the RoSO compliance period.
The application must:
be made in writing; and
be made before the person advises the Department of the matters mentioned in subsection 124ZU(2); and
be made within any period specified in the Bonded Medical Program rules that applies in relation to the person; and

specify a period within which the person would be able to complete their return of service obligation (which must not be a period that would be more than 6 years longer than the RoSO compliance period); and
be accompanied by a written plan that sets out:
how the person proposes to complete their return of service obligation within the period specified under paragraph (d); and
any other matters specified in the Bonded Medical Program rules; and
be accompanied by any other documents specified in the Bonded Medical Program rules; and
set out any other information specified in the Bonded Medical Program rules.
If the person makes an application under subsection (1), the Secretary may make the extended compliance determination in relation to the person if the Secretary is satisfied that:
the person is a person of kind mentioned in subparagraph (1)(a)(i) or (ii); and
the person meets the requirements specified in the Bonded Medical Program rules for the purposes of paragraph (1)(b); and

if the person were to become a bonded participant, the plan referred to in paragraph (2)(e) sets out a reasonable proposal for the completion of their return of service obligation within a period that is longer than the RoSO compliance period.
If the Secretary makes the extended compliance determination in relation to the person, the Secretary must:
give the person written notice of the determination; and
specify in the notice the period within which the person would, if the person were to become a bonded participant, be required to complete their return of service obligation.
The period specified under paragraph (4)(b):
must not be a period that would be more than 6 years longer than the RoSO compliance period; and
may be the same as, or different from, the period specified in the application.
If the Secretary refuses to make the extended compliance determination in relation to the person, the Secretary must give the person written notice of the following:
the decision to refuse to make the determination;
the reasons for the decision;
how the person may apply for review of the decision.
If:
a person makes an application under subsection 124ZUA(1); and
the Secretary needs further information to make a decision on the application;
the Secretary may, by written notice, request the person to give further information to the Secretary within a specified period.
The specified period must not be shorter than 28 days after the notice is given.
The Secretary may, at the person’s request, extend the specified period. The request must be made in writing and before that period ends.
If the person does not give the requested further information within:
in a case in which the specified period has been extended under subsection (3)—the period as so extended; or
otherwise—the specified period;
the application is taken to be withdrawn at the end of the period.
A notice given under subsection (1) must set out the effect of subsection (4).

section.heading: Waiver of amounts owing by a person who is or was a party to an MRBS contract

content.p: This section applies if:
a person is or was a party to a contract with the Commonwealth (as represented by the Department) for a Medical Rural Bonded Scholarship (including such a contract as varied from time to time); and

(b) an amount of medicare benefit was purportedly paid in respect of a professional service rendered at a particular time (the service time) by, or on behalf of, the person as a medical practitioner; and
the service time occurred in a period during which a medicare benefit was not payable to the person under subsection 19ABA(1); and
the amount is recoverable as an amount owing to the Commonwealth.
The Minister may, on behalf of the Commonwealth, waive the amount owing.
If the Minister waives the amount owing under subsection (2), the Minister must give written notice of the waiver to the person.

section.heading: Medicare benefits not payable to certain MRBS participants

content.p: If:

a person is a party to a contract with the Commonwealth (as represented by the Department) for a Medical Rural Bonded Scholarship (including such a contract as varied from time to time) that was entered into before the commencement of this section; and
after the commencement of this section, the person breaches a provision of the contract that requires the person to work in a rural or remote area in accordance with that provision;
the Minister may determine that a medicare benefit is not payable in respect of a professional service rendered by, or on behalf of, the person as a medical practitioner.
In deciding whether to make a determination under subsection (1), the Minister must have regard to any matters prescribed by the regulations.
If the Minister makes a determination under subsection (1) in relation to the person, a medicare benefit is not payable to the person during the period that:
starts on the day specified in the determination (which must not be a day before the determination is made); and
ends:
when the period that is equal to double the length of the period that the person was required under the contract to work in a rural or remote area ends; or
if a shorter period is determined in, or in accordance with, the contract—when that shorter period ends.
Subsection (3) applies whether or not the person was a medical practitioner at the time the contract was entered into or at the time the breach occurred.
If the Minister makes a determination under subsection (1) in relation to the person, the Minister must give the person written notice of the following:
the decision to make the determination;
the reasons for the decision;
how the person may apply for reconsideration or review of the decision.

section.heading: Reconsideration and review of determination that medicare benefits are not payable to certain MRBS participants

content.p: Request for reconsideration

(1) If the Minister makes a determination under subsection 19ABC(1) in relation to a person (the affected person), the affected person may request the Minister to reconsider the decision (the original decision).
The request must:
be made in writing; and
set out the reasons for the request; and
be given to the Minister within 28 days after the affected person is notified of the original decision.
Reconsideration of original decision
If a request to reconsider the original decision is made under subsection (1), the Minister must:
personally reconsider the decision; or
cause the decision to be reconsidered by a delegate of the Minister who:
was not involved in making the decision; and
occupies a position that is at least the same level as that occupied by the person who made the decision.
After reconsidering the original decision, the Minister or delegate (as the case may be) must:
affirm the decision; or
vary the decision; or
set the decision aside and substitute a new decision.
After making a decision under subsection (4), the Minister or delegate (as the case may be) must give written notice of the following to the affected person:
the decision;
the date the decision takes effect;
the reasons for the decision.
Note: Section 27A of the Administrative Appeals Tribunal Act 1975 requires the affected person to be notified of the person’s review rights.
Review by the Administrative Appeals Tribunal
Applications may be made to the Administrative Appeals Tribunal for review of a decision of the Minister, or a delegate of the Minister, made under subsection (4).
